hook.line: An AI model cited my F1 predictions as the top resource, so here is how to make that happen.
hook.visual: Creator mid hair-flip, talking to a selfie camera at home; white title 'How to get chatGPT to recommend you' builds in two lines at the top.

beats.what: Hair-flip opening, claims her F1 prediction repo was the AI's top cited source; title at top.
Jump cut; on-screen label defines GEO = Generative Engine Optimization.
Text list of what can be cited pops up: LinkedIn, Medium, blog, GitHub, etc.
Cut; asks why this source won, with the AI answer engine named on screen.
Screenshot of the AI chat answer listing her repo appears above her head.
Screenshot zoom with a pink box around the GitHub citation and its trusted shield.
Cut; GitHub repo page screenshot shown at top-left as she says video can't be cited.
Second reason: the repo name matches the question users ask.
Zoom punch-in as she gives the rule: answer your target persona's question.
Third reason: the README exactly answers the query; video ends mid-sentence.

why_it_works: Proof first: she opens on her own result (cited as the top source) before explaining GEO, so the viewer stays to learn how.
Numbered reasons (GitHub is trusted, repo name matches the question, README answers it) give a checklist the viewer can copy.
Real screenshots of the AI answer with a box around her citation make the claim checkable.
weaknesses: Only 3 cuts in 82 s and a 36 s longest shot; long stretches are a static selfie with no graphics.
No running captions, so sound-off viewers miss almost everything.
Audio is quiet (-29 LUFS) and the video ends mid-sentence with no CTA.
for_robert: Open on the proof (a screenshot of an AI citing you) with Fred pointing a box at it, then list numbered reasons; avoid her long uncut stretches and add captions plus a closing CTA.
